Mr. Sandipan Ganguly, Sr. Adv. Mr. Ayan Bhattacharya Mr. Anirban Datta Mr.
Tanay Agarwal Mr. Shivam Bhimsaria ..for the petitioner Learned senior counsel on behalf of the petitioner submits as follows:-

The petitioner has prayed for quashing of proceedings being CGR No.2677 of 2018 corresponding to Karaya Police Station Case No.334 of 2018 dated 23 rd June, 2018 under Sections 120B/403/406/420/506 of the Indian Penal Code presently pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate at Alipore as well as the order of taking cognizance.

entities.text: Karaya Police Station Case No.334 of 2018
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Indisputably, the petitioner is Ex-Director of M/s. Chetki Properties Pvt. Ltd.
There was an agreement between the Company of the petitioner and the opposite party No.2 to sell a particular property.

In the said agreement of sale executed between the petitioner's company and the opposite party No.2 there is a specific clause under Clause No.12.8 which runs as follows:-
"The Confirming Party and the Developer can go for sanction of extra floor on the said building and /or for sanction of space for shops/commercial purposes in the ground floor and the purchaser will have no objection there for so long as the purchaser's area of the said Unit is not affected thereby."
It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that as per the said agreement possession was delivered to the private opposite party in respect of the their purchase portion.

However, on 23rd June, 2018 the opposite party No.2 lodged a complaint in the jurisdictional P.S. alleging, inter alia, that the petitioner had committed an offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code by constructing an additional floor over the said premises making provisions for some shops and other establishments etc. in violation of the agreement.
I am prima facie satisfied that such allegation cannot stand in view of the specific clause No.12.8 in the agreement for sale executed by and between the parties.
Charge under Sections under Sections 120B/403/406/420/506 of the Indian Penal Code is also questionable because delivery of property has already been made.
The petitioner is directed to serve notice upon the private opposite parties under registered speed post with A/D and file affidavit of service within three weeks from the date of this order.
The State of West Bengal be served through the learned Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta.
